title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 43 (Kinds of Share Capital)

content.overview: Section 43 provides that the share capital of a company limited by shares shall be of two kinds, namely:—(a) equity share capital—(i) with voting rights; or (ii) with differential rights as to dividend, voting or otherwise in accordance with such rules as may be prescribed; and (b) preference share capital. Provided that nothing contained in this Act shall affect the rights of the preference shareholders who are entitled to participate in the proceeds of winding up before the commencement of this Act. Explanation: equity share capital means all share capital which is not preference share capital; preference share capital means that part of the issued share capital which carries or would carry a preferential right with respect to (a) payment of dividend, either as a fixed amount or an amount calculated at a fixed rate, which may either be free of or subject to income-tax; and (b) repayment, in the case of a winding up or repayment of capital, of the amount of the share capital paid-up or deemed to have been paid-up, whether or not there is a preferential right to the payment of any fixed premium or premium on any fixed scale specified in the memorandum or articles.
content.glance: Equity (with voting rights or prescribed differential rights) vs preference (preferential dividend and preferential capital repayment); pre-commencement participating preference rights preserved.
content.study: Share capital of a company limited by shares is of two kinds: equity and preference. Equity is all capital that is not preference, and may carry voting rights or differential rights as to dividend, voting or otherwise in accordance with prescribed rules. Preference capital carries preferential rights as to dividend (fixed amount or rate) and as to repayment of capital on winding up or repayment of capital. Pre-commencement preference rights to participate in winding-up proceeds are preserved. Current-law framing: examine rights attached; classify equity or preference; if differential equity, test prescribed rules.

sections.heading: Two kinds
sections.body: Share capital of a company limited by shares: equity share capital or preference share capital.

sections.heading: Equity share capital
sections.body: All share capital which is not preference; may carry voting rights or differential rights as to dividend, voting or otherwise in accordance with prescribed rules.

sections.heading: Preference share capital
sections.body: Preferential right to dividend (fixed amount or rate) and preferential right to repayment of capital on winding up or repayment of capital.

sections.heading: Pre-commencement rights
sections.body: Nothing in this Act affects the rights of preference shareholders entitled to participate in the proceeds of winding up before the commencement of this Act.

examples.title: Ordinary equity
examples.body: Shares with ordinary voting rights and residual dividend rights are equity share capital.

examples.title: Preference classification
examples.body: Shares with fixed preferential dividend and priority capital repayment on winding up are preference share capital under s. 43.

hypotheticals.question: How do you classify shares with fixed preferential dividend and priority capital repayment?
hypotheticals.analysis: They fall within preference share capital under s. 43 when the statutory preferential rights as to dividend and capital are present.

misconceptions.trap: Any share with a higher dividend is automatically preference capital.
misconceptions.correction: Preference status depends on the statutory preferential rights as to dividend and repayment of capital specified in s. 43.
